result.title: CAPE-JEPA - Cross-modal Adversarial Probabilistic Embedding JEPA
result.comment: Accepted for publication at the British Machine Vision Conference (BMVC 2026)
result.summary: Cross-modal remote sensing image retrieval (RS-CMIR) requires representations that are simultaneously modality-invariant and semantically discriminative, despite the profound physical gap between heterogeneous sensors such as Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and multispectral imagery. Recent JEPA-based Predictive self-supervised approaches such as X-JEPA formulate cross-modal alignment as a deterministic latent forecasting task, implicitly assuming uniform patch predictability and leaving cross-modal distributional alignment unaddressed. We propose CAPE-JEPA, a probabilistic cross-modal Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture with three contributions: (i) a cross-attentional Gaussian predictor outputting per-patch parameters (mu, sigma^2) conditioned on opposite-modality context, trained via negative log-likelihood to model inherent cross-sensor prediction uncertainty; (ii) adversarial distributional regularization combining unimodal isotropic Gaussian regularization with a novel cross-modal adversarial variant that aligns modality distributions via worst-case Epps-Pulley characteristic function tests without explicit sample pairing; and (iii) in-training contrastive learning with attention-pooled heads for scene-level discriminative grounding. Evaluated on BigEarthNet-14K (BEN-14K) and fMoW across SAR, multispectral, and RGB modalities, CAPE-JEPA surpasses X-JEPA by up to 13.74 points on BEN-14K and 15.59 points on fMoW, outperforming all baselines including SkySense and CROMA across both unimodal and cross-modal directions while using fewer parameters (407.30M vs. 432.72M).

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CAPE-JEPA，用于 SAR、多光谱与 RGB 遥感图像的跨模态检索：以跨注意力高斯预测器输出逐 patch 的均值与方差并按负对数似然训练，配合基于 Epps-Pulley 特征函数检验的跨模态对抗式分布正则以及训练期对比学习。
AI.relevance_reason: 其概率化 latent 预测与不确定性估计可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态的置信度刻画、视觉证据筛选与停止决策提供可核查线索，但该文面向检索对齐，未涉及推理轨迹生成或答案对 latent 内容的使用。
